newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent jumps as Shell trims Nigerian output.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent jumps as Shell trims Nigerian output.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures jumped 20 cents late on Friday after news that fresh ethnic clashes in Nigeria had forced Shell to reduce production, brokers said.
June Brent climbed to $18.52 a barrel, 11 cents up on the day but still three cents off the session high, before easing back to $18.45 a barrel by 1731 GMT.
Dealers said the market rallied after Shell said it was forced to shut in about 20 percent of production at Forcados, equivalent to about 90,000 barrels per day (bpd).
But prices eased back after the Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) said no cargoes had been cancelled, they said.
NNPC said Forcados cargoes scheduled to load from April 29 to May 6 had been put back by two days. Lifters of Forcados loading from May 7-20 had been informed of a three-day delay, he added.
Renewed clashes in Nigeria's oil-producing swamps between militant youths of rival tribes have claimed many lives and forced Shell to close its Warri flowstation last weekend.
June Brent also drew strength from an earlier break through resistance at $18.39 a barrel which propelled the contract to intraday highs, brokers said.
Support was seen at $18.20 a barrel, they said.
Earlier, IPE gas oil closed stronger in thin volume, having spent most of the day tracking crude.
May IPE gas oil last traded 75 cents higher at $165.50 a tonne, having earlier tested but failed at resistance of $167.00.
